intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February 2026

experiences.name: Skiing on Zermatt's Matterhorn Glacier Paradise
experiences.description: Ski the world-famous slopes surrounding the iconic Matterhorn peak. With over 360km of marked runs, this is one of the finest ski experiences in the world. Take the cable car to Klein Matterhorn at 3,883m for breathtaking panoramic views and access to year-round glacier skiing. Suitable for intermediate to advanced skiers.

experiences.name: Jungfrau Region Ski Safari
experiences.description: Explore the legendary Jungfrau ski region connecting Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren across 213km of pristine pistes. Ride the historic cogwheel railway to Jungfraujoch — the 'Top of Europe' at 3,454m — for stunning views over the Aletsch Glacier. A must-do multi-resort ski adventure with iconic Swiss Alpine scenery.

experiences.name: St. Moritz Bobsled Run Experience
experiences.description: Ride the world's oldest natural ice bobsled track, the Cresta Run, in the glamorous resort town of St. Moritz. As a passenger on a professional bob, reach speeds of up to 130km/h on this legendary 1.7km track carved from natural ice. A thrilling once-in-a-lifetime winter adrenaline experience with deep Alpine heritage.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Raclette Fondue Evening
experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with a traditional Swiss mountain dinner in a cozy chalet restaurant. Indulge in authentic raclette and cheese fondue made with local Gruyère and Emmental, paired with Swiss wines or hot Glühwein. Many chalets in Verbier offer live folk music, making this a rich cultural and culinary Alpine experience.

experiences.name: Snowshoeing and Ice Climbing in Engelberg
experiences.description: Discover the quieter side of the Swiss Alps with a guided snowshoeing trek through pristine snow-covered forests and frozen waterfalls near Engelberg. Add an introductory ice climbing session on a frozen cascade with a certified mountain guide. This immersive experience combines adventure, nature, and Alpine culture away from the crowded ski resorts.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 13:00. Take the SBB Swiss Federal Railways train from Zurich Airport to Visp (approx. 2.5 hours, ~CHF 50 with a Swiss Travel Pass or saver ticket booked in advance). From Visp, board the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn (MGB) narrow-gauge train to Zermatt (approx. 1.5 hours, ~CHF 15). Check in to your Boutique Stay accommodation in Zermatt. Note: Zermatt is a car-free village — no private vehicles allowed, so enjoy the peaceful alpine atmosphere on arrival.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely stroll through Zermatt's charming pedestrian main street (Bahnhofstrasse) to get oriented. Admire the first views of the iconic Matterhorn peak. Visit the free outdoor viewpoints near the village center for photos at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport or grab a snack on the train — pick up a sandwich or pretzel from a Migros or Coop kiosk at Zurich Airport or Visp station (~CHF 5–8)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch or grab a quick bite at Visp train station Coop or kiosk (~CHF 8–12)
meals.dinner: Brown Cow Pub & Restaurant, Zermatt — budget-friendly pub grub, burgers and pasta from ~CHF 18–25. Casual, warm atmosphere perfect after a long travel day.

day_by_day.notes: Book SBB train tickets in advance at sbb.ch for the best saver fares. The Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn leg from Visp to Zermatt is scenic — sit on the right side of the train for mountain views. Zermatt is at 1,608m altitude — stay hydrated and rest well on arrival night to acclimatize.

day_by_day.morning: First full day on the slopes! Head to the Sunnegga Paradise ski area — one of Zermatt's most accessible and budget-friendliest zones. Take the underground Sunnegga Express funicular (included with ski pass) up to 2,288m. Enjoy beginner to intermediate ski runs with stunning Matterhorn views. Rent ski equipment from one of Zermatt's rental shops (Sport Julen or Slalom Sport) — book online in advance for ~CHF 35–45/day for skis, boots, and poles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Sunnegga or venture up to Blauherd (2,571m) via cable car for more varied intermediate runs. Try the Kumme ski area pistes — wide, well-groomed runs ideal for building confidence. Take a break at a mid-mountain restaurant terrace to soak in the panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village by 16:30. Warm up at your accommodation, then explore the free Zermatt village walking trail along the Vispa river. Visit the small but free Zermatt village church and the old Hinterdorf quarter with traditional Walliser log houses.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast at accommodation using groceries from Migros supermarket in Zermatt (~CHF 5–8) — bread, cheese, cold cuts, yogurt
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch or eat at Sunnegga mountain restaurant — go for the soup of the day and bread (~CHF 12–16) rather than full meals to save money
meals.dinner: Whymper-Stube, Zermatt — famous for its affordable Swiss fondue and raclette, portions from ~CHF 20–28. A true Swiss alpine experience without breaking the budget.

day_by_day.notes: A 1-day Zermatt ski pass costs approximately CHF 80–90 for adults. Consider buying a multi-day pass (3–7 days) for significant savings — a 6-day pass is roughly CHF 380–420. Sunnegga area is best for value and less crowded than Cervinia-linked runs. Altitude at ski areas reaches 3,883m — apply high SPF sunscreen even on cloudy days.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Rothorn ski area today — take the Sunnegga Express then the Blauherd gondola up to Rothorn at 3,103m. Enjoy spectacular high-alpine skiing with views across the Swiss and Italian Alps. The Rothorn area offers excellent intermediate and advanced red runs. Ski the Kumme and Triftji pistes — among Zermatt's best value-for-money terrain.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, try the Leisee lake area near Sunnegga — in winter this small frozen lake area offers a scenic flat ski-back route and is great for photos with the Matterhorn perfectly framed. Alternatively, take a free snowshoe walk around the Leisee area (snowshoe rental ~CHF 15/day from village shops) if you want a break from ski boots.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Zermatt Matterhorn Museum (Zermatlantis) — entry ~CHF 10. It tells the fascinating story of the first Matterhorn ascent in 1865 and the history of alpinism. Well worth the modest entry fee. Afterward, browse the duty-free-style alpine gear shops along Bahnhofstrasse.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — oats, fruit, and Swiss milk from Migros (~CHF 4–6)
meals.lunch: Chez Vrony at Findeln (mid-mountain, accessible by ski) — splurge slightly on their famous homemade soups and rösti (~CHF 22–30). One of the best mountain lunches in Zermatt with iconic Matterhorn views.
meals.dinner: Coop supermarket self-catered dinner — buy ready-made raclette cheese, potatoes, and pickles (~CHF 12–15 total). Use the accommodation kitchen for an authentic Swiss dinner at a fraction of restaurant prices.

day_by_day.notes: The Matterhorn Museum is closed on certain days — check opening hours at matterhornmuseum.ch before visiting. Chez Vrony is ski-in/ski-out from the Findeln area runs and is a legendary budget-splurge lunch spot — reservations recommended even at lunch. The Rothorn area can be windy — bring a neck gaiter and goggles.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Klein Matterhorn (Matterhorn Glacier Paradise) — the highest cable car station in the Alps at 3,883m. Take the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise cable car from Zermatt (included in ski pass or ~CHF 100 without ski pass — budget carefully). Ski on Europe's highest ski terrain and the Klein Matterhorn glacier. The views from the panoramic platform are absolutely breathtaking — on clear days you can see Mont Blanc and the Dolomites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski back down via the long, scenic Weisse Perle (White Pearl) run — one of the most iconic descents in the Alps, going from 3,883m all the way back toward Zermatt village (12km, 2,200m vertical drop). Take your time and enjoy multiple rest stops. If snow conditions allow, this run takes 2–3 hours at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recovery evening — your legs will need it after the Weisse Perle! Soak in the accommodation if facilities are available, or visit the Alpentherme Leukerbad (requires travel — save for another day). Instead, do a gentle evening walk through Zermatt village, visit the English Church (free entry), and browse the atmospheric lit-up village streets.

meals.breakfast: Hearty self-catered breakfast before the big glacier day — eggs, toast, cheese, and Swiss hot chocolate (~CHF 6–8)
meals.lunch: Trockener Steg mountain restaurant (3,488m) — go for the daily soup special and a bread roll (~CHF 14–18). Eating at altitude feels like a real alpine adventure.
meals.dinner: Pizzeria Roma, Zermatt — reliable, filling Italian pizzas and pasta from ~CHF 16–22. One of Zermatt's best value sit-down dinner options.

day_by_day.notes: The Matterhorn Glacier Paradise cable car can have long queues — arrive at the cable car base by 08:30 to beat the crowds. Dress in extra warm layers — at 3,883m it can be -15°C or colder even in February. The Weisse Perle run is rated blue/red — suitable for confident intermediate skiers. Check weather forecasts the night before as the glacier area closes in poor visibility.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day from skiing — explore Zermatt's free outdoor winter activities. Take a free self-guided hike on the winter walking path from Zermatt village up toward Furi (1,864m) — about 1.5 hours uphill through snowy forest and alpine meadows. The path is well-marked and free to use. Stunning Matterhorn views throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try free sledding — rent a sled from a local sports shop (~CHF 10/half day) and use the public toboggan run near Furi. Alternatively, take the free village ice skating rink at the Oberdorf area (skate rental ~CHF 8). Visit the free Gornergrat viewpoint lower area — walk the marked winter trail from Riffelalp for panoramic views without paying the full Gornergrat rack railway fare.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the free weekly Zermatt village events — check the Zermatt Tourism board (zermatt.ch) for free concerts, torchlight ski descents, or alpine demonstrations that often happen on Friday evenings in February. The torchlight ski descent by ski school instructors is a spectacular free show.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — Swiss muesli with yogurt and berries from Migros (~CHF 4–5)
meals.lunch: Grab a takeaway Wurst (bratwurst) and rösti from a village kiosk or food stand (~CHF 10–14). Eat outdoors by the Vispa river for a scenic budget lunch.
meals.dinner: Hotel Bahnhof restaurant or similar village local eatery — try the Zermatt staple of Käseschnitte (Swiss cheese toast) or Älplermagronen (alpine mac and cheese) from ~CHF 16–20.

day_by_day.notes: Friday evenings in Zermatt can be lively with weekenders arriving — village atmosphere is excellent. The Zermatt Tourism Office on Bahnhofplatz offers free maps, trail guides, and event listings — stop in to pick up the weekly events calendar. Rest day is important mid-trip to prevent muscle fatigue for the final ski days.

day_by_day.morning: Final big ski day — tackle the Gornergrat area today. Take the famous Gornergrat rack railway (Brig-Visp-Zermatt line) up to Gornergrat at 3,089m (~CHF 44 return without ski pass, or included in ski pass). The railway itself is a UNESCO-recognized experience with incredible panoramic views of 29 four-thousand-meter peaks. Ski the Riffelberg and Riffelalp area runs — excellent intermediate terrain with classic Swiss alpine scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski the long Gornergrat to Riffelalp to Zermatt descent — a beautiful 13km run back to the village. Stop at the Riffelberg Hotel terrace for a hot chocolate break with views of the Gorner Glacier. In the afternoon, try the Stockhorn area (3,532m) if conditions allow — accessed from Gornergrat — for more challenging off-piste adjacent terrain.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your last full ski day with a slightly bigger dinner splurge. Walk the festive Bahnhofstrasse one final time, pick up any Swiss souvenirs from the Migros or Coop (Swiss chocolate is the best budget souvenir — ~CHF 3–5 per bar). Check and pack ski rental equipment for return tomorrow morning.

meals.breakfast: Hearty self-catered breakfast — pack extra snacks for the mountain day (~CHF 6–8)
meals.lunch: Kulmhotel Gornergrat restaurant (3,089m) — the highest hotel in the Alps! Treat yourself to their soup and sandwich lunch deal (~CHF 20–25). The views from the terrace are once-in-a-lifetime.
meals.dinner: Walliserkanne, Zermatt — a Zermatt institution offering traditional Valais cuisine. Try the Valais meat platter or cheese fondue (~CHF 25–35). Slightly above daily budget but worth it for the last evening.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day in Zermatt as weekend visitors arrive — hit the slopes early (lifts open 08:00) to beat queues. The Gornergrat railway is very popular — buy tickets online in advance at gornergrat.ch. Return ski rental equipment by 18:00 to avoid extra charges. Pack ski gear and prepare luggage for Sunday departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Zermatt — wake up early for one last sunrise view of the Matterhorn from the village. Take a short free walk to the Matterhorn viewpoint at the cemetery (Bergsteigerfriedhof) — the mountaineers' graveyard is a moving and historically significant free site with direct Matterhorn views. Check out of accommodation by 11:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn from Zermatt to Visp (depart around 11:30–12:00, ~CHF 15). Connect at Visp to the SBB InterCity train toward Zurich Airport. Journey takes approximately 2.5–3 hours to Zurich Airport. Arrive at Zurich Airport with plenty of time for your departure. Browse the Zurich Airport duty-free for last-minute Swiss chocolate and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Zurich Airport. Reflect on an incredible week of budget alpine adventure in the Swiss Alps — world-class skiing, stunning Matterhorn views, and authentic Swiss culture experienced without overspending.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast — use up remaining groceries from Migros (~CHF 4–6). Make it a good one!
meals.lunch: Grab lunch at Visp or on the train — Coop or Migros kiosk sandwich and drink (~CHF 10–14)
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Zurich Airport — Coop Restaurant or Marché at the airport offers reasonably priced hot meals (~CHF 18–25) before your flight

day_by_day.notes: Budget Summary Estimate for 7 days: Accommodation (6 nights boutique stay) ~CHF 600–900 total depending on room type; 6-day ski pass ~CHF 380–420; ski rental ~CHF 210–270 (6 days); train transport (Zurich-Zermatt return) ~CHF 130; food/meals ~CHF 280–350 (mix of self-catering and budget restaurants); activities/museums ~CHF 30–50. TOTAL ESTIMATE: ~CHF 1,630–1,990 (approx. USD 1,800–2,200) for the full week. Top money-saving tips: buy multi-day ski passes, self-cater breakfasts and some dinners, book trains in advance on sbb.ch, and use the free Zermatt village activities generously.

trip_options.title: Classic Swiss Alps, Switzerland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Travel from the airport to Zermatt via train (Zurich/Geneva → Visp → Zermatt). Zermatt is car-free, so take the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn from Visp for the final leg. Enjoy the scenic mountain views on the way in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Zermatt (~15:30–16:00 estimated). Check in to the Boutique Stay in Zermatt, Valais. Freshen up, unpack, and take a leisurely stroll along the Bahnhofstrasse to get oriented. Visit the Zermatt village center, browse ski rental shops, and book/confirm equipment rentals for the following days.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming village on foot. Visit the small but fascinating Matterhorn Museum (Zermatlantis) to learn about the history of Alpine mountaineering — a perfect low-key introduction to the region.

meals.breakfast: Onboard the flight or at the airport — no formal breakfast stop planned.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Zurich HB or Geneva airport during the transit connection — try a Migros or Aperto café for a sandwich and coffee (~CHF 12–18).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Whymper-Stube in Zermatt — a cozy, mid-range chalet-style restaurant known for its fondue and Swiss classics. Budget ~CHF 35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is accessible only by train (no private cars allowed). Pre-book ski rental from a shop like Intersport or Slalom Sport to save time on Day 2. The altitude (~1,608m) may cause mild fatigue — hydrate well and rest early to acclimatize.

day_by_day.morning: Full day on the slopes — Skiing on Zermatt's Matterhorn Glacier Paradise. Start early with a gondola ride up to Klein Matterhorn (3,883m), the highest ski area in the Alps. Ski the upper glacier runs in crisp morning conditions when snow is best. Enjoy breathtaking views of the Matterhorn up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing the Zermatt ski area, focusing on the Rothorn and Sunnegga sectors. These mid-mountain areas offer a variety of blue and red runs ideal for all levels. Take a scenic break at a mountain restaurant around 13:00–14:00 before hitting afternoon runs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village by gondola (~16:30). Rest and freshen up at the boutique hotel. Take a relaxed walk through the village as the golden-hour light hits the Matterhorn — one of the most photographed moments in Switzerland.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby bakery such as Bäckerei Fuchs — croissants, muesli, and coffee. Budget ~CHF 10–15.
meals.lunch: Mountain lunch at Chez Vrony on the Findeln slope — a beloved mid-mountain restaurant with stunning Matterhorn views. Try the rösti or mountain soup. Budget ~CHF 25–40.
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Raclette Fondue Evening experience — book a traditional Swiss mountain dinner at a cozy chalet restaurant in Zermatt such as Restaurant du Pont. Raclette and cheese fondue with local wine. Budget ~CHF 40–60 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a multi-day Zermatt ski pass in advance online for savings (3–6 day passes offer better value). Wear SPF 50+ sunscreen — UV radiation is intense at glacier altitude. Ski helmets are strongly recommended and available at rental shops.

day_by_day.morning: Second full day skiing in Zermatt — focus on the Gornergrat sector today for a different experience. Take the historic Gornergrat Bahn (cog railway) up to 3,089m for panoramic views of 29 four-thousand-meter peaks. Ski the wide, groomed red and blue runs on this side of the mountain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski down to Riffelalp or Riffelberg and explore intermediate runs in this quieter sector. For those wanting a break from skiing, the Gornergrat viewpoint offers one of the finest mountain panoramas in Europe — a great spot for photography. Ride the train back down to the village by 16:00.
day_by_day.evening: Snowshoe walk around the illuminated village of Zermatt in the early evening — a magical experience as the Matterhorn glows under moonlight. Many marked snowshoe paths are accessible directly from the village.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — a full Swiss-style spread with cold cuts, cheese, bread, and yogurt. Typically included or ~CHF 15–20 if à la carte.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Riffelberg (mid-mountain) — hearty Alpine dishes like goulash soup, Bratwurst, or pasta. Budget ~CHF 22–35.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Schäferstube inside the Hotel Julen — a warm, rustic atmosphere serving traditional Swiss cuisine with a modern twist. Budget ~CHF 40–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wednesday is typically less crowded on the Gornergrat sector — a good day to explore this area. The Gornergrat Bahn is a tourist experience in itself and is included with the Zermatt ski pass. Book dinner reservations in advance as popular spots fill quickly in peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Jungfrau Region Ski Safari. Take an early train from Zermatt to Grindelwald (via Visp and Interlaken, ~2.5–3 hours). Begin skiing the famous Jungfrau ski area, starting from Grindelwald-First or the Männlichen plateau. Enjoy the iconic views of the Eiger North Face.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Jungfrau Ski Safari, traversing toward Wengen or exploring the connecting runs between Grindelwald and Lauberhorn. The legendary Lauberhorn downhill race course is accessible to confident intermediate skiers. Take the Wengernalp Railway back toward Grindelwald by 15:30.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to Zermatt by train (~2.5 hours). Arrive back at the hotel by 19:30–20:00. Enjoy a quieter evening with a short walk and an early dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab a pastry and coffee at Zermatt train station before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Brandegg or a mountain hut on the Jungfrau slopes — try the local Älplermagronen (Alpine macaroni) or a warming soup. Budget ~CHF 20–32.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at Papperla Pub in Zermatt — a lively après-ski pub with hearty food options like burgers, pizza, and Swiss snacks. Budget ~CHF 25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a day ski pass for the Jungfrau region separately (~CHF 85–95 for a one-day adult pass). The train journey is scenic and counts as part of the experience — sit on the right side heading toward Interlaken for the best Eiger views. Start early to maximize skiing time given travel.

day_by_day.morning: Snowshoeing and Ice Climbing in Engelberg experience — take an early train from Zermatt toward Engelberg (via Visp and Lucerne, ~3 hours). Join a guided snowshoeing trek through pristine powder fields in the Engelberg valley with views of the Titlis glacier. A certified guide leads the group through off-piste terrain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in an introductory ice climbing session on a frozen waterfall near Engelberg with the guide — equipment provided. This is a thrilling and accessible experience for beginners and intermediate adventurers alike. Return to Engelberg village by 15:30.
day_by_day.evening: Return train to Zermatt (arriving ~19:00–19:30). Relax at the hotel with a hot shower. Spend the evening reflecting on the week's adventures with a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or a stop at a local mountain café in Engelberg — try Hüttenkäse (mountain cheese) sandwiches and hot chocolate. Budget ~CHF 15–25.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Stockhorn in Zermatt — a relaxed mid-range spot with excellent fondue and a warm chalet atmosphere. Budget ~CHF 38–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Engelberg snowshoeing and ice climbing guided experience in advance through a local operator like Bergführer Engelberg. Dress in warm, waterproof layers. The train journey through central Switzerland via Lucerne is exceptionally scenic. This is a great active recovery day from intensive skiing.

day_by_day.morning: St. Moritz Bobsled Run Experience — travel from Zermatt to St. Moritz by train (via Chur on the Glacier Express or regional trains, ~3.5–4 hours). Arrive in St. Moritz and head to the legendary Cresta Run, the world's oldest natural ice bobsled track. Experience a thrilling ride down the 1,212-meter track at speeds up to 130 km/h.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the glamorous village of St. Moritz on foot. Visit the frozen Lake St. Moritz where various winter sports take place. Browse the upscale village — window-shopping along Via Serlas is free and entertaining. If time allows, take a scenic horse-drawn carriage ride on the frozen lake.
day_by_day.evening: Return train journey to Zermatt (arriving ~19:30–20:00). Final evening in the Alps — celebrate the trip with a special dinner at one of Zermatt's finest mid-range restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before the early departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch in St. Moritz at Hauser's Café & Restaurant — a St. Moritz institution since 1921 with excellent pastries, soups, and light meals. Budget ~CHF 28–42.
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at Restaurant Elsie's in Zermatt — a beloved local institution known for oysters, snails, and Swiss wine in an intimate setting. Budget ~CHF 50–70 per person. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Cresta Run experience requires advance booking and has age/weight restrictions — check eligibility on the St. Moritz Tobogganing Club website. Saturday trains can be busier — book seats in advance. The Glacier Express route (even partially) is one of the most scenic rail journeys in the world and worth the scenic route if time permits.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Zermatt — rise early for one last sunrise view of the Matterhorn from the village (Matterhorn View Bridge is a perfect free spot). Take a gentle final ski run or a relaxed snowshoe walk on the Sunnegga area for a peaceful send-off. Return ski equipment to the rental shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the boutique hotel (standard checkout 11:00 — arrange luggage storage if needed). Take the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn from Zermatt back toward Visp and onward to your departure airport. Enjoy the final scenic train ride through the Valais valley.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland. If the flight is late evening, spend time at the airport or nearby city (Zurich/Geneva) exploring a café or doing last-minute Swiss chocolate and souvenir shopping at the airport duty-free.

meals.breakfast: Final Swiss breakfast at the hotel — enjoy it slowly and savor the Matterhorn views one last time.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Visp or the departure airport — try a Birchermüesli or a Gipfeli (Swiss croissant) with coffee. Budget ~CHF 12–20.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or onboard the return flight — Zurich and Geneva airports have excellent food halls with Swiss and international options. Budget ~CHF 20–35.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3.5–4 hours of travel time from Zermatt to Zurich airport (or ~2.5 hours to Geneva airport). Zermatt's car-free policy means all luggage must be manageable on trains. Pick up Swiss chocolate, Läderach pralines, and local cheese at Zermatt shops or the airport as souvenirs. Validate all train tickets before boarding.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

A must-do multi-resort ski adventure with iconic Swiss Alpine scenery.

experiences.name: St. Moritz Bobsled Run Experience
experiences.description: Ride the world's oldest natural ice bobsled track, the Cresta Run, in the glamorous resort town of St. Moritz. As a passenger on a professional bob, reach speeds of up to 130km/h on this legendary 1.7km track carved from natural ice. A thrilling once-in-a-lifetime winter adrenaline experience with deep Alpine heritage.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Raclette Fondue Evening
experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with a traditional Swiss mountain dinner in a cozy chalet restaurant. Indulge in authentic raclette and cheese fondue made with local Gruyère and Emmental, paired with Swiss wines or hot Glühwein. Many chalets in Verbier offer live folk music, making this a rich cultural and culinary Alpine experience.

experiences.name: Snowshoeing and Ice Climbing in Engelberg
experiences.description: Discover the quieter side of the Swiss Alps with a guided snowshoeing trek through pristine snow-covered forests and frozen waterfalls near Engelberg. Add an introductory ice climbing session on a frozen cascade with a certified mountain guide. This immersive experience combines adventure, nature, and Alpine culture away from the crowded ski resorts.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Travel time from airport (Zurich or Geneva) to Zermatt via private transfer and Zermatt shuttle train is approximately 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chauffeured transfer from the airport to Zermatt. Check in to your boutique luxury stay in Zermatt, Valais. Settle into your suite, enjoy a welcome amenity, and take a leisurely stroll through Zermatt's car-free village centre to get oriented. Visit the iconic Matterhorn viewpoint at Riffelberg for a first dramatic glimpse of the peak.
day_by_day.evening: Orientation dinner at Restaurant Chez Vrony on the slopes above Findeln — one of Zermatt's most celebrated mountain restaurants. Enjoy regional Valais wines, house-made charcuterie, and hearty Alpine cuisine with panoramic Matterhorn views as the sun sets. Early night to prepare for skiing the next morning.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at the airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light snack or airport lounge meal during transit
meals.dinner: Restaurant Chez Vrony, Findeln — à la carte Alpine cuisine with premium Valais wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Zermatt is car-free; luggage is transported by electric taxi from Täsch. Confirm early check-in with the hotel if possible. Pack ski gear or confirm rental arrangements for Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day skiing on Zermatt's Matterhorn Glacier Paradise. Begin with a private ski guide meeting at your hotel at 08:30. Take the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise cable car — the highest cable car station in the Alps at 3,883m — and begin your descent on the legendary Klein Matterhorn runs. Your guide will tailor the route to your skill level across Zermatt's 360km of marked pistes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing through the Italian-Swiss border runs toward Cervinia for a cross-border lunch experience. Explore the Theodul Glacier area and the scenic Gornergrat ridge runs in the afternoon. Optional heli-skiing add-on can be arranged through your guide for untouched powder terrain.
day_by_day.evening: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Raclette Fondue Evening at a private chalet dining experience. A dedicated fondue and raclette dinner at Whymper-Stube, a legendary Zermatt institution serving traditional Valais raclette and cheese fondue in a cosy timber-beamed setting. Pair with a crisp Swiss Fendant white wine.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet hotel breakfast — freshly baked breads, Swiss cheeses, charcuterie, eggs to order, fresh juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at Riffelhaus 1853 on the Gornergrat — panoramic terrace dining with Alpine soup, rösti, and grilled meats
meals.dinner: Whymper-Stube, Zermatt — traditional raclette and fondue with Valais wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Book private ski guide at least 48 hours in advance through the hotel concierge. Altitude acclimatisation is important — stay hydrated and take it steady on Day 1 of skiing. Lift pass (Zermatt All-In) should be purchased or pre-loaded onto a card. Heli-skiing requires weather clearance.

day_by_day.morning: Snowshoeing and Ice Climbing in Engelberg — full-day excursion. Depart Zermatt by private transfer (approx. 2.5 hours) to Engelberg, a pristine Alpine resort beneath Mount Titlis. Begin with a guided snowshoeing trek through the Hahnen valley, traversing untouched snow-covered forests and frozen meadows with a certified mountain guide. The quieter, more meditative side of the Swiss Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition to a beginner-to-intermediate ice climbing session on a frozen waterfall near Engelberg with a certified UIAGM mountain guide. Full equipment — crampons, ice axes, harness — provided. Suitable for first-timers with a full safety briefing. Spectacular icy canyon scenery throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Return by private transfer to Zermatt (arrive approx. 20:00). Relaxing dinner at The Omnia's fine dining restaurant — a clifftop luxury property with sweeping Matterhorn views. Enjoy a tasting menu of contemporary Alpine cuisine with a curated Swiss wine list.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by your guide in the Engelberg backcountry — thermos soups, artisan sandwiches, Swiss chocolate
meals.dinner: The Omnia Restaurant, Zermatt — contemporary Alpine tasting menu with Swiss and international wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Engelberg day trip is approximately 5–6 hours of activity. Private transfers recommended for comfort and flexibility. Dress in moisture-wicking base layers with waterproof outer shells. Ice climbing is physically demanding — inform the guide of any fitness or health considerations in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfrau Region Ski Safari — full-day excursion. Private transfer to Grindelwald (approx. 2 hours from Zermatt). Begin your ski safari on the legendary Jungfrau ski region, connecting Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren across 213km of immaculate pistes. Start on the First mountain above Grindelwald with sweeping Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the ski safari via the Kleine Scheidegg saddle toward Wengen and Mürren. Ski the famous Lauberhorn descent — the course of the world's longest downhill World Cup race. A private guide ensures seamless navigation across the interconnected resort areas and helps you find the best groomed runs and off-piste opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Grindelwald before private transfer back to Zermatt. Reserve a table at Restaurant Schmitte — a sophisticated mountain brasserie with locally sourced Bernese Oberland ingredients, craft Alpine cocktails, and a warm, intimate atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Bellevue des Alpes, Kleine Scheidegg — a historic mountain hotel with classic Swiss cuisine and extraordinary Eiger views
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schmitte, Grindelwald — contemporary Swiss brasserie with regional produce and Alpine-inspired cocktails

day_by_day.notes: The Jungfrau ski region requires a separate lift pass (Top Ski Pass). Your concierge can arrange this in advance. The Lauberhorn run is a red/black gradient — confirm suitability with your guide. Allow 2 hours for the return transfer to Zermatt after dinner.

day_by_day.morning: St. Moritz Bobsled Run Experience — full-day excursion. Private transfer to St. Moritz (approx. 3 hours from Zermatt). Arrive at the legendary Cresta Run — the world's oldest natural ice bobsled track, established in 1884. Receive a full safety briefing and equipment fitting before experiencing the thrill of riding a steel skeleton sled at speeds exceeding 130km/h down the 1,212-metre ice channel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore glamorous St. Moritz at leisure. Browse the luxury boutiques along Via Serlas — Cartier, Bulgari, Hermès — or visit the Engadine Museum for insight into the region's aristocratic winter heritage. Optional: take the Corviglia cable car for an afternoon ski session on St. Moritz's sun-drenched south-facing slopes.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Badrutt's Palace Hotel's La Diala restaurant — one of Switzerland's most iconic fine dining addresses. Enjoy a seasonal tasting menu with Engadine truffle, Alpine venison, and an extraordinary cellar of Burgundy and Barolo. Private transfer back to Zermatt after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Kulm Hotel's sunny terrace restaurant — classic Engadine cuisine with panoramic Lake St. Moritz views
meals.dinner: La Diala at Badrutt's Palace Hotel, St. Moritz — haute cuisine tasting menu with sommelier-led wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Cresta Run is open to non-members through organised guest experiences — book well in advance as slots are extremely limited. Minimum age is 18. The experience is weather and ice-condition dependent. St. Moritz is approximately 3 hours from Zermatt; an early 07:00 departure is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning in Zermatt. Sleep in and enjoy an extended gourmet breakfast at the hotel. Mid-morning private guided ski touring session on the quieter, off-piste terrain above Zermatt with a certified mountain guide — explore the Stockhorn or Schwarzsee areas away from the weekend crowds. Breathtaking solitude and powder.
day_by_day.afternoon: Après-ski and relaxation. Return to Zermatt village by 13:30. Enjoy the hotel's spa facilities — sauna, steam room, heated indoor pool, and a 60-minute deep-tissue sports massage to recover tired muscles. Alternatively, explore Zermatt's charming village: the Matterhorn Museum Zermatlantis, local artisan shops, and the historic English church.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-to-skiing celebration dinner at Restaurant Zum See — a legendary, remote Zermatt chalet restaurant accessible only on foot or by ski. Reserve a candlelit table in the rustic timber dining room. The menu is driven by local Valais produce — game, Alpine herbs, artisan cheese — paired with rare Swiss Pinot Noir. One of Zermatt's most magical dining experiences.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury hotel breakfast — champagne, pastries, eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, Swiss cheeses
meals.lunch: Light post-skiing lunch at Snowboat, Zermatt — lakeside Alpine café with gourmet sandwiches, soups, and craft drinks
meals.dinner: Restaurant Zum See, Zermatt — legendary remote chalet dining with Valais cuisine and rare Swiss wines

day_by_day.notes: Restaurant Zum See requires advance reservation (often weeks ahead) and is only accessible via a 20-minute walk or ski. Your hotel concierge should book this on Day 1 of the trip. The spa should also be pre-booked. Ski touring requires appropriate avalanche safety equipment — provided by the guide.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Zermatt. Enjoy a leisurely final breakfast at the hotel. Take a gentle morning walk through the village to the Matterhorn cemetery — a poignant and beautiful tribute to Alpine climbers — and pause for a last coffee at one of Zermatt's sunlit café terraces with Matterhorn views. Pack and check out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chauffeured transfer from Zermatt to Zurich Airport (approx. 3.5 hours via Täsch and motorway). Depending on departure time, stop en route at the charming town of Brig or Visp for a final Swiss lunch. Alternatively, enjoy the airport's Swiss premium lounge before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland. Reflect on an extraordinary week in the Swiss Alps from the comfort of your business or first-class cabin.

meals.breakfast: Final luxury hotel breakfast — take your time and savour the last Matterhorn views
meals.lunch: Either a farewell lunch at a local Brig restaurant en route (Restaurant Walliserkanne recommended) or premium airport lounge dining at Zurich
meals.dinner: In-flight dining on departure

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3.5–4 hours travel time from Zermatt to Zurich Airport. Check out by 11:00 (confirm late checkout with hotel if needed). Arrange luggage collection and Täsch car park or shuttle in advance. Ensure all ski rental equipment is returned by Day 6 evening or early Day 7 morning to avoid additional charges.
